hypothesis: QQQ mean-reverts after closing below its 20-day lower Bollinger Band, but only in low-volatility regimes (current 20d realized vol <= trailing 1yr median); high-vol regimes are explicitly excluded because the prior SMA-crossover strategy (2026-09-01-001) failed walk-forward specifically due to regime-dependence around the 2022 rate-hike period.
rejection_reason: Sharpe ratio -0.30 vs required >= 1.0, a clear (non-borderline) fail on full-sample data (2019-2026, QQQ). Only 14 trades / 81 days in market over 7.7 years; strategy lost money on a risk-adjusted basis. Remaining validators (transaction costs, walk-forward, parameter sensitivity) skipped per RESEARCH_LOOP.md Step 5/6: a negative full-sample Sharpe cannot pass a stricter out-of-sample check, so running them would not change the outcome.
notes: Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY SMA crossover, trend-following, rejected on walk-forward) and 2026-09-02-001 (BTC funding-rate mean reversion, rejected on data feasibility) -- this is a QQQ mean-reversion idea with an explicit vol-regime filter designed to avoid exactly the regime-dependence that broke 2026-09-01-001. Vol-regime filter worked as intended (kept MDD to 15%, low market exposure), but the underlying entry signal itself has no discernible edge on QQQ daily bars. Two ideas for a future loop, recorded in the backtest report: (1) try a coarser Bollinger band (2.5-3 std) / shorter timeframe to get a stronger per-trade edge with fewer, higher-conviction trades; (2) the full-sample annualized Sharpe metric may unfairly penalize any low-market-exposure strategy during QQQ's 2019-2026 secular uptrend -- a days-in-market-only comparison could be a fairer validator refinement. Also fixed two real scaffold bugs this loop: vectorbt import was broken by plotly>=5.24 removing scattermapbox (pinned plotly<5.24 in requirements.txt), and validators.py check_sharpe_ratio/check_max_drawdown crashed with "Index frequency is None" (fixed by passing freq="D" explicitly to the vectorbt returns accessor).
